editorial: The hush of a cemetery lures you into a darkness that feels almost tangible. The horror reframes a gruesome affliction as a family secret buried beneath stones, turning each dig into a moral test. A standout is the film’s use of long, claustrophobic tracking shots that bleed into the unearthly glow of the cursed remains, making the supernatural almost tactile. Ideal for viewers who savor atmospheric dread and nuanced character dynamics over jump scares. Despite its initial slow-burn, Exhuma (2024) pulls the tension into a tense collapse that sometimes drags in the final quarter when the plot settles back into routine investigation.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
